As an operator, you’ll work in the hub of an innovative recycling company that transforms old foam materials into new end products such as carpet underlays and insulation panels. The products are dismantled at other locations, and the recycled material is returned to the Alphen aan den Rijn site as large foam blocks (up to 5,500 kilos each). That’s where your work begins. You’ll be responsible for operating various machines in the production line, including the flake mill, mixing chamber, pouring cylinder, and laminating machine. You’ll also handle the timely supply of raw materials and semi-finished products using a forklift. No forklift certificate yet? No problem, you can obtain it through Luba.The company works with two shifts, but you will only work the evening shift, from 15:00 to 00:00. As the company is growing rapidly, the work environment is dynamic and developing. The day shift currently consists of 15 employees, while the evening shift has just 3. You will be part of the growing evening shift, which will eventually expand to a team of around 15 people, with all five machines operating, just like during the day shift.During the process, the foam is shredded, glued, steamed, and laminated. You make sure the right materials are available, machines are running properly, and you take action when needed. You work carefully and keep your workplace clean and safe. Together with your colleagues, you ensure everything runs smoothly and efficiently. Wetsus logo  CampusAcademy  Oostergoweg 9 8911 MA Leeuwarden +31 (0)58 284 30 00 info@wetsus.nl  msc thesis/intership project: sequential degradation/transformation of organic micropollutants in aerobic-anaerobic conditions Type of project : MSc Thesis/internship Anticipated start : from Jan/Feb 2027 Duration: >5 months Location: Wetsus, European center of excellence for sustainable water technology (Leeuwarden, the Netherlands) Project description: In the Netherlands, 60% of the drinking water is produced from groundwater. To ensure future groundwater extraction, aquifers must be actively recharged with surface water to maintain sufficient groundwater. However, this must occur without introducing organic micropollutants (OMPs) from surface water in the aquifer. Engineered nature-based systems like constructed wetlands can remove OMPs effectively. The aim of this project is to explore the OMP removal capacity of redox-specific microorganism communities which naturally forms in a wetland system by performing a bottle experiment. Fig.1 Constructed wetlands act as a barrier between surface water and managed aquifer recharge (specifically described as natural infiltration) Tasks : - Manipulate headspace gas and available electron acceptors to create and maintain active microorganisms' community under different redox conditions in bottle experiments. - Spike targeted OMPs into bottles, sample these bottles regularly to track the removal of OMPs. - Prepare samples for LC-MS, LC-OCD and anions measurement. - Data analysis. - Writing a report. Your profile: - Background in environmental science/technology/engineering, chemistry, or related fields. - Basic experience or knowledge in batch degradation/adsorption study is required. - Established hands-on laboratory and instrument experience would be a plus. - Analytical skills in LC-MS and LC-OCD will be a plus. - Fluent in English and good English writing skills - EU citizen or...
